description: Capabilities for both AccessibleAudioStudio Pro window types as of 0.2.0: the persistent main Recording Studio window (label "main") and every dynamically-created editor window (labels "editor-1", "editor-2", ... — one per open audio document, created at runtime via tauri::WebviewWindowBuilder, so a wildcard pattern is required here rather than listing labels that don't exist yet; confirmed as the correct, sanctioned approach directly from Tauri's own multi-window documentation). Almost the entire app calls no Tauri commands at all — microphone access, recording, playback, and storage are all standard web APIs (getUserMedia, MediaRecorder, IndexedDB) handled by the WebView2 runtime, not Tauri IPC. The main window's Open Audio and New Audio create editor windows (open_audio_windows, open_new_editor_window); each editor window then calls get_editor_init_info once, on load, to fetch its own document; both window types call set_shared_audio_clipboard/get_shared_audio_clipboard for cross-window Copy/Paste. Open Audio itself still shows Windows' classic Explorer-style multi-select file dialog (GetOpenFileNameW) via the windows crate directly, not any Tauri plugin, with a dialog hook intercepting Ctrl+V inside the dialog's File Name field — unchanged since 0.1.8. Custom app commands registered via invoke_handler are allowed by default for every window under core:default — no plugin-specific permission entry is needed for any of them. This app has not depended on any Tauri dialog or fs plugin since 0.1.4/0.1.5, so no dialog:* or fs:* permissions are granted here. Window creation itself (open_audio_windows, open_new_editor_window) happens inside these custom commands' own Rust code calling tauri::WebviewWindowBuilder directly — not via Tauri's frontend-initiated webview-creation IPC command — so it needs no core:webview:allow-create-webview-window grant either, the same reasoning already established for every other custom command in this app.
